Picodash

Picodash is a React package family for adding configurable controls, readouts, visualizations, and
movable tool panels to existing applications.

Status:
- Store, UI, DashPanel, DashList, and Picodash initial target contracts: accepted.
- Current source and tests: working prototypes, not automatic compatibility requirements.
- Product implementation: ready to begin with Store after the documentation baseline commit.

Products:
- @picodash/store: framework-independent typed values, atomic validation, scoped metadata,
  persistence, import/export, diagnostics, and external-value adapters.
- @picodash/store/react: public React hooks and typed selectors.
- @picodash/store/integration: advanced shared context and declarative lifecycle leases.
- @picodash/dashpanel: standalone DashPanelProvider and DashPanel shell with configurable docking.
- @picodash/dashlist: standalone DashList, DashGroup, Dashlet, binding, and reorder composition;
  Dashlet and DashGroup IDs are explicit and independent of field bindings.
- DashList and DashGroup direct children are one-to-one List node declarations. DashList permits
  Dashlets and one level of DashGroups; DashGroups contain Dashlets only at initial launch.
  Arrays/fragments flatten; arbitrary wrappers and registered descendants inside a Dashlet are
  invalid.
- The public Dashlet shell owns registration, binding, ordering, and accessible identity. Optional
  Dashlet anatomy is non-registering content inside that shell.
- Reorderability is a DashList/DashGroup container policy applied uniformly to immediate children;
  Dashlets do not expose `reorderable` or create fixed barriers within pin bands. DashList defaults
  to reorderable; DashGroup inherits that policy unless it explicitly overrides its child
  container.
- `pin="start"` and `pin="end"` are declarative node classifications; omission selects the automatic
  band. Nodes never reorder across bands, and pin classification is not persisted user state.
- Pointer and keyboard reorder previews remain ephemeral; a changed order commits once, while
  cancellation and no-op sessions write nothing. DashList owns the shared reorder live region.
- Collapse belongs to DashGroup only at initial launch. Collapsed descendants stay mounted and
  registered while their content becomes inert and unavailable to accessibility APIs.
- Disabled/read-only policies cascade to Dashlet content but remain separate from reorder,
  disclosure, authorization, and external Store writes. Read-only does not disable unbound actions.
- Safe-area Dashlet clicks focus an explicit primary target or the named `tabIndex={-1}` shell.
  Compound Dashlets nominate the target; DOM scanning is not part of the target contract.
- Labels, descriptions, and field issues attach to the actual Dashlet controls. Dirty draft discard
  is separate from canonical reset; generic shell `status`/`states` props remain Draft.
- Compound Dashlets map normalized issues by alias, unique field, then canonical field path;
  ambiguous and cross-field issues belong to the named Dashlet composition.
- DashList owns generic ready-made Dashlets and their catalog metadata. DashPanel owns no Dashlets;
  Picodash may reexport them and aggregate package catalogs without copying entries. Initial
  Picodash owns no ready-made Dashlet or extra family. A future Picodash component must coordinate
  Panel and List behavior; dependency-heavy optional families use separate packages.
- Catalogs are deeply frozen JSON-compatible discovery data for Accepted public components. They
  contain no React values, registration, loaders, prop schemas, token inventories, or query API.
  Picodash aggregates exact owner entries and records facade paths as reexports.
- DashList owns and exports List behavior actions. Expand/Collapse all target active collapsible
  groups in one List scope and commit once; Picodash composes the same exports into integrated menus.
- The action surface is useDashListActions(scopeId?), DashListActionItems, named expand/collapse
  items, and named Reset submenu/items. Omission targets nearest Store scope; an explicit scope stays
  within the same root. Availability is unavailable, disabled, or enabled. Built-in reset items
  repeat confirmation if the displayed effect changes.
- Action execution returns not_executed with unavailable/disabled state or executed with the Store
  CoreTransactionResult or PersistentTransactionResult. Transaction rejection remains structured;
  contract errors throw.
- Standalone document exports are useDashListDocumentActions(scopeId?), DashListDocumentItems,
  DashListExportItem, and DashListImportItem. They operate on one current-scope JSON document with
  no descendants. Store owns plans and validation; DashList owns browser I/O and review UX;
  initial Picodash reuses the primary-List workflow without inferred additional-List aggregation.
  Initial UI has no field/scope mapping or missing-scope creation.
- DashList separates `Reset values…` from `Reset list…`: the first resets current-List registered
  values and targeted drafts, while the second removes order/collapse overrides without changing
  values. DashList has no combined Reset all action.
- Initial ready-made DashList exports are Text, Number, Slider, Switch, Select, Segmented, and
  Display Dashlets. Anatomy, unbound UI, and catalog metadata use `/dashlet`, `/ui`, and `/catalog`.
- DashList `/ui` exports exactly TextField, NumberField, Slider, Switch, Select, SegmentedControl,
  and Display. There is no initial Picodash `/advanced` or `/dashlet`, DashPanel `/advanced` or
  `/ui`, or UI catalog. Draft anatomy is `@experimental` and excluded from catalogs.
- Ready-made Dashlets require explicit id, typed field, and visible label. Store owns defaults and
  validation; configuration is passed as ordinary React props, and incompatible presentations never
  silently write canonical values.
- Invalid ready-made props are contract errors. Valid but unrepresentable Store values produce an
  ephemeral presentation warning that shows the real value and requires explicit replacement.
- Ready-made-specific props cover text shape, numeric bounds/formatting, explicit Slider marks,
  unique string-or-number choices, and Display formatting. No implicit choice fallback, children,
  or arbitrary inner-control prop bags.
- DashList rows respond to their container through shared handle/label/control/trailing tracks;
  groups establish new grids, compact rows stack, and drag previews preserve captured geometry.
- Rail presentation represents Dashlets as named icons in a vertical or horizontal strip. Built-ins
  supply type icons, groups retain disclosure behavior, and an active scoped Store orientation wins
  over a DashList prop. Picodash forces main side docks vertical and main top/bottom docks horizontal;
  corner, free, and snapped Panels publish no Picodash orientation override.
- At a corner, effective Store or prop orientation selects the rail's physical edge. Picodash-only
  arena allocation gives same-axis corner pairs halves, lets perpendicular rails stop at one
  another's inner edges, and gives two corners plus a main rail thirds. These caps are transient.
- Long press enters transient rail reorder mode and reveals eligible handles. Dashlet icon activation
  pauses while group disclosure continues; children of a non-reorderable group appear without
  handles. Accessible Reorder/Done controls, Escape, and outside dismissal remain required.
- Density is `regular | compact`, orthogonal to color theme, inherited through theme context, and
  repeated on detached roots. Compact changes geometry, preserves coarse hit targets, and is not
  persisted automatically.
- Compact is not a theme. UI alone owns light/dark and regular/compact recipes. The Picodash
  stylesheet aggregates owning styles once and defines no facade theme. Named custom themes provide
  all 24 shared color tokens plus color-scheme in host CSS; website themes are not package exports.
- Drawer and sheet are host-selected transient modal DashPanel presentations. They preserve desktop
  placement, permit one visible sibling modal per Provider, require visible Close, and implement
  documented focus, dismissal, backdrop, scroll, portal, and width behavior.
- DashPanel width resolves from inherited `--picodash-panel-width` and then the per-Panel `width`
  prop. Intrinsic CSS widths are supported and boundary-capped; resolved width is not persisted.
- @picodash/picodash: integrated facade after Store, DashPanel, and DashList stabilize.
- @picodash/ui: supporting theme, density, token, structural CSS, and generic accessible UI
  foundation shared by DashPanel and DashList. The former @picodash/theme package was retired in
  the pre-release clean replacement; it is not a second target authority.
- PicodashThemeProvider resolves color theme and density. The independent
  PicodashOverlayProvider supplies portal and layer defaults. Product Providers compose both;
  detached roots repeat resolved theme and density without mutating a shared portal container.
- AlertDialog/modal confirmation primitives are canonically imported from @picodash/ui;
  @picodash/picodash/ui may explicitly reexport them. Current product-local copies are prototypes.

- TESTING.md: test-layer policy.

Core Store contract:
- One root owns canonical field values and durable scope metadata.
- root.scope(scopeId) returns an immutable view of the same authority.
- Scopes organize trusted state and attribution; they do not restrict field access.
- Snapshots contain immutable data and commands live on Store APIs.
- Binding input uses parse, Standard Schema canonicalization, and validation. Other sources skip the
  UI parser and use schema plus validation.
- Store-owned mode persists permitted application values and Picodash metadata.
- External-owned mode uses one synchronous root adapter and persists Picodash metadata only.
- Persistence, document, repair, overwrite, and prune recovery use explicit root-owned plans.
- DashPanel and DashList register active entities and relationships through declarative leases.
- DashPanel dock occupancy and allocation are transient Provider runtime; Store persists only
  settled placement and preferred boundary-relative free position.
- Imperative Panel deregistration is retired.

Workspace applications:
- apps/web: production evaluation website; / is the only public route.
- apps/lab: local Contract Lab at /lab and checked-in visual audit reports.

Verification:
- bun install
- vp check
- vp run -r test
- vp run -r build
- bun run test:e2e:lab:cap
- bun run test:e2e:lab
- bun run test:e2e:web
- bun run ready

Run the narrowest owning check first. Use browser tests only for behavior requiring a real browser.
